extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of American government; legislators and civics educators
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for judging the quality of Acts of Congress and for understanding how congressional committees affect legislative outcomes and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: The excellence of the substance of a bill
rubrics_metrics.description: The excellence of the substance of a bill, i.e. its tendency to improve the law and promote the public welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a primary test of legislative quality; the text contrasts English practice where important (government) bills are carefully weighed by the ministry with American practice. The implication is that bills backed by responsible executive draftsmen and political responsibility tend to have better substantive policy judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: The excellence of the form of a bill
rubrics_metrics.description: The excellence of the form of a bill, i.e. its arrangement and the scientific precision of its language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form matters: English government bills are prepared by official draftsmen (an office of two eminent lawyers and assistants) producing precise language; private members often must employ counsel. Poor drafting in committees or hurried processes undermines clarity and legal precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: The harmony and consistency of an act with the other acts of the same session
rubrics_metrics.description: The harmony and consistency of an act with the other acts of the same session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committees working independently tend to produce legislation that lacks relation to other measures, producing a 'patchwork quilt' rather than coherent policy. Evaluators should check for policy consistency across acts in the same session.

rubrics_metrics.name: The due examination and sifting in debate of a bill
rubrics_metrics.description: The due examination and sifting in debate of a bill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A bill should be thoroughly debated and sifted. The chapter notes that committee-centred procedure and limited House time 'cramp' debate in the House of Representatives, so assess whether sufficient public and parliamentary debate occurred before enactment.

rubrics_metrics.name: The publicity of a bill
rubrics_metrics.description: The publicity of a bill, i.e. the bringing it to the knowledge of the country at large, so that public opinion may be fully expressed regarding it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicity is diminished when committees deliberate in secret and reports are terse. Newspapers rarely report committee evidence unless public interest is high. Evaluate how widely the bill was publicized and whether the public had a real chance to weigh in.

rubrics_metrics.name: The honesty and courage of the legislative assembly in rejecting a bill
rubrics_metrics.description: The honesty and courage of the legislative assembly in rejecting a bill, however likely to be popular, which their judgment disapproves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether legislators act according to judgment rather than short-term popularity. The text contrasts English ministers (who risk office) with U.S. practice where dispersed responsibility makes courageous rejection less likely.

rubrics_metrics.name: The responsibility of some person or body for the enactment of a measure
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsibility of some person or body of persons for the enactment of a measure, i.e. the fixing on the right shoulders of the praise for passing a good, the blame for passing a bad, act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good legislative systems make clear who is accountable. The passage argues that U.S. committee delegation diffuses responsibility (no single ministry to blame), reducing political accountability; evaluate whether responsibility is identifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee gatekeeping power over bills
rubrics_metrics.description: Committees can take evidence, hear advocates and opponents, amend the bill, and can practically extinguish a bill by reporting adversely, delaying to report till late, or not reporting at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nearly nineteen-twentieths of introduced bills die in committee. This gatekeeping is decisive for legislative fate; evaluate committee hearings, amendments, timeliness of reporting, and whether committee action reflected thorough consideration or mere obstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee deliberations: secrecy and reporting practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The deliberations of committees are usually secret; evidence may be taken with open doors but newspapers do not report it unless the matter excites public interest; reports are often curt and do not state how members voted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy affects transparency, publicity, and accountability. Assess whether committee proceedings were sufficiently open, whether reports disclosed reasoning and votes, and whether rules were followed (e.g., it is out of order to canvass committee proceedings in the House until formally reported).

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee composition and method of selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee membership is nominated at the beginning of each Congress, practically selected by party caucuses (e.g., Ways and Means) and approved by the House; sizes vary and members usually sit on more than one committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The composition determines the character of measures in a policy area. Evaluate whether committees include appropriate expertise and balanced representation; note that the best members are concentrated on a few great committees while others are composed of ordinary members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chairmen's power and influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Power is thrown into the hands of the chairmen of committees, especially those dealing with finance and great material interests; they become practically a second set of ministers and can determine policy of the branch they oversee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chairmen wield de facto authority though often without corresponding public responsibility. Evaluate the extent of chairmen's informal power, methods (secret or public), and effects on legislation and departmental behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time constraints on committee reports and House consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: One hour is allowed to the member appointed to report; he seldom uses the whole hour and usually moves the previous question, precluding subsequent amendments and leaving only an hour before the vote. On average each committee has only two hours of House time in a ten-month Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Severe time limits constrain amendment and debate. Assess whether these procedural time constraints allowed meaningful consideration or forced hurried, superficial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of labor enabling handling of many measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Dividing the assembly into smaller committees enables the handling of a far greater number of measures than the whole House could consider and permits taking evidence by those who will reshape or amend a bill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a practical advantage: committees allow scrutiny of administrative departments and specialized work suited to members' training. Evaluate whether the division of labor improved technical scrutiny despite its other costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of underhand and corrupt influence (log-rolling and lobbyists)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a small committee the voice of each member is well worth securing and may be secured with little danger of public scandal; the arrangements of the committee system have produced and sustain professional 'lobbyists' and facilitate reciprocal jobbing ('log-rolling').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess vulnerability to corruption: number of secret meetings, difficulty for press/nation to follow many committee rooms, and whether suspicious bargains were possible and later concealed by hurried House proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on unity, cohesion, and the scope of debate
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee system destroys the unity of the House as a legislative body, cramps real debate, and lessens cohesion and harmony of legislation; each committee proceeds as though legislating for a separate sphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether committee-centric processes have shifted the center of gravity away from plenary debate and whether legislation shows lack of coherent policy or wide-ranging deliberation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation of responsibility and public accountability caused by committee system
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee system reduces responsibility because the ministry does not sit in Congress and the House often follows a committee decision, making it hard to blame the dominant party; the committee may be obscure and members insignificant to be blamed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether political accountability for enacted measures is diffuse and whether that diffusion affects incentives for good lawmaking; consider whether scandals are the only way responsibility is brought home.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee scrutiny of administrative departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative committees can summon officials, interrogate them as to methods and conduct, and require minute reports, thereby closely scrutinizing the working of departments; authority is limited since officials answer to the President, who may refuse to allow appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the effectiveness of committees' oversight of executive departments: were officials examined, were reports produced, and did scrutiny lead to corrective legislation or guidance despite limits on compulsory power?

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee role in initiating and shaping legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: Technically committees have no right to initiate a bill, but they can transform a referred bill or procure one to be brought in and referred to them; thus the character of measures depends on committee composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the extent of committee-driven legislation: whether committees effectively originate major proposals, how they reshape referred bills, and the implications for democratic deliberation and representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee effectiveness in killing worthless bills
rubrics_metrics.description: Under this system the House despatches a vast amount of work and does the negative part of it — the killing off of worthless bills — in a thorough way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize this as a positive evaluative dimension: despite drawbacks, committees filter out the bulk of unworthy proposals. When evaluating legislative quality, weigh filtering benefits against costs in debate, cohesion, and accountability.
